# matcher.search_cqp { #polars_corpus.matcher.search_cqp }

```python
matcher.search_cqp(df, query)
```

Search corpus using a CQP-style query.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type         | Description            | Default    |
|--------|--------------|------------------------|------------|
| df     | pl.DataFrame | Corpus to be searched. | _required_ |
| query  | str          | CQP query string       | _required_ |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type          | Description          |
|--------|---------------|----------------------|
|        | SearchResults | Result of the search |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                          |
|--------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------|
|        | ParseException | If there's an error in the query                     |
|        | RuntimeError   | If there's an internal error in the search procedure |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

For CQP query syntax documentation, see the CQP documentation.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> search_cqp(corpus, '[word="fox"]')
>>> search_cqp(corpus, '[pos="NN.*"]+ [pos="VB.*"]')
```
